water-loading-hydration-maxxing.text: Users drink large amounts of water in the belief that it plumps skin and reduces facial puffiness. It is a common fixture of skincare and depuffing routines. Fixed targets such as eight glasses are not backed by research, and the appearance effect specifically is largely anecdotal.

16-8-time-restricted-eating.text: Users adopt a daily 8-hour eating window as a simple structure for eating less and getting leaner, which they link to a sharper face and body. Trials have measured weight and metabolic markers rather than appearance, so the look-based claims rest on that fat-loss pathway.

alternate-day-fasting.text: Followers use alternate-day fasting as a route to rapid fat loss and a leaner face and physique. Trials show weight loss, comparable to ordinary calorie restriction, while appearance outcomes themselves have not been the focus of research.

5-2-diet.text: People use the 5:2 pattern as a flexible way to create a calorie deficit and lose fat, with the aim of a leaner physique. Studies show weight loss similar to standard dieting; appearance outcomes have not been the research focus.

fasting-mimicking-diet.text: The fasting-mimicking diet is promoted in longevity circles for slowing biological aging, which some users hope shows up as better skin and a leaner look. It has been studied for aging markers and disease risk, not for visible appearance.

dry-fasting.text: Some wellness and looksmaxxing circles advocate dry fasting for rapid fat loss, a leaner face and clearer skin. Research covers religious daytime fasts such as Ramadan; the appearance claims for longer dry fasts are anecdotal.

bulking.text: Lifters bulk to add muscle size, giving a broader, more muscular physique before a later cut. Eating a calorie surplus alongside resistance training is a well-studied route to gaining muscle, with debate centring on how much fat comes with it.

dirty-bulk.text: Users dirty bulk to gain size quickly without tracking food closely, accepting extra fat that is cut afterward. It is contrasted with clean bulking, and forum posters discuss it especially among steroid users. Comparisons of the two are mostly based on lifter experience.

lean-bulk.text: Lean bulking is used to add muscle slowly while staying lean enough to keep a defined face and physique. It rests on the studied link between a calorie surplus, training and muscle gain; the exact surplus that limits fat gain is mostly lifter lore.

cutting.text: Cutting is a staple of looksmaxxing leanness advice, used to lose fat so facial bone structure and muscle definition become visible. Calorie deficit reliably reduces body fat; forum claims about how face appearance changes at low body fat are anecdotal.

leanmaxxing.text: Leanmaxxing is often the first step in looksmaxxing, aimed at revealing cheekbones and the jawline by losing body fat. Fat loss reducing facial fullness is widely observed; the exact body-fat levels cited on forums come from anecdote.

chain: Fat loss and muscle gain together
recomp.text: Recomp is used mainly by beginners and skinny-fat lifters aiming to lose fat and build muscle at once, improving shape without separate bulk and cut phases. It is studied in trained and untrained groups, while forum protocols with drugs are largely anecdotal.

mini-cut.text: Lifters use mini-cuts of a few weeks to shed recent fat between bulking phases, restoring definition without a long diet. It applies the established calorie-deficit pathway to fat loss; the specific 2 to 6 week format is lifter convention.

chain: Leaner or fuller face and body
calorie-counting.text: Looksmaxxers count calories to control cutting and bulking precisely, mainly to get lean enough to show facial and body definition. Tracking is a studied aid to weight change, while claims that it is the most reliable route to a leaner face are anecdotal.

macro-tracking-iifym.text: Lifters track macros, often under the flexible IIFYM approach, to drive cutting or bulking toward a defined physique. Protein and calorie targets are well studied; research on macro tracking itself as a method is limited.

protein-shakes-whey.text: Users drink whey shakes to hit protein targets for muscle building and recovery, supporting a more muscular, leaner frame. Protein supplementation alongside training is well studied for muscle gain; no studies look at facial appearance.

gallon-of-milk-a-day-gomad.text: GOMAD comes from strength circles and is discussed by looksmaxxers as a way to add mass quickly, for a bigger frame. It relies on the general link between a calorie surplus and weight gain; the named protocol itself has not been tested.

big-dirty-bulk-fast-food-bulking.text: Users eat a very large surplus of calorie-dense fast food to gain mass quickly, planning to cut fat afterward. Faster scale gains are reported by lifters; comparisons with cleaner bulks rest mostly on anecdote.

eating-for-jaw-chewing-hard-foods.text: Users chew tough foods hoping to enlarge the masseters and sharpen the jawline, alongside mastic gum and jaw exercisers. The masseter can enlarge with heavy chewing, but hard-food diets themselves have not been tested for visible jaw change.

low-carb-to-lose-face-puffiness.text: People go low-carb, sometimes briefly before a photo or event, to drop water weight and look leaner in the face. The shift in glycogen-bound water is well described; face-specific results have not been studied.

chain: Alternating high and low carb days
Fuel for training, lower weekly calories
carb-cycling.text: Physique athletes and lifters use carb cycling to fuel hard training while dieting, aiming for fat loss with muscle kept. Direct trial evidence for advantages over steady dieting is limited, and claims about leptin come largely from practitioners.

refeed-days-diet-breaks.text: Dieters schedule refeeds or diet breaks during a cut to look fuller and sustain fat loss. They are common in bodybuilding and appearance-focused circles; research on them is thin and metabolic claims are mostly anecdotal.

chain: Shifts in water under the skin
Drier, more defined look on the day
sodium-potassium-manipulation-peak-week.text: Bodybuilders adjust sodium, potassium and fluids in the final days before a show or shoot to look drier and more defined. It is documented as part of contest prep; controlled evidence for the visual effect is limited.

water-cutting-dehydration-pre-photo.text: Competitors and photo-minded users restrict fluids shortly before a shoot or contest to look drier and more defined. It appears as the last stage of bodybuilding prep; the visual benefit is reported by practitioners rather than measured in trials.

whole-food-unprocessed-diet.text: Users switch to minimally processed foods hoping for leanness, less facial bloating and better skin. Observational studies link ultra-processed food to weight gain and health outcomes; no trials test skin or face appearance.

clean-eating.text: Clean eating, the chicken, rice and broccoli staple, is used in forums for clearer skin and a leaner look. Its health effects have limited research and links to disordered eating have been flagged; skin claims are mostly anecdotal.

eat-the-rainbow-skin-nutrient-diet.text: Users eat varied colourful produce for vitamins and antioxidants, hoping for better skin. Carotenoid intake has been linked to skin colour, while antioxidant supplement trials showed no benefit; the colour approach itself has no skin studies.

oatmeal-fibre-for-gut-skin-axis.text: Users eat oats and other fibre to feed gut bacteria in the hope of clearer skin, via a proposed gut-skin axis. Fibre has documented gut and cholesterol effects; skin benefits are untested.

probiotics-fermented-food-for-skin.text: People take probiotics or eat kefir and kimchi hoping to clear acne and calm skin, based on a proposed gut-skin link. Acne research is described as preliminary, with some evidence in eczema.

chain: Eliminating triggers, adding probiotics and fibre
gut-health-protocols-gut-skin-axis.text: Users bundle food elimination, probiotics, fermented foods and fibre to clear skin through the gut. Gut-skin links are mostly associations; no trials of the bundled protocols were found.
